package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5 and earlier (approximate, as per public reporting)
package_info.why_malicious: The Orion software update mechanism was compromised to deliver a malicious backdoor (Sunburst) to customers. The update contained injected code within a legitimate DLL that enabled attackers to gain persistent, covert access to victim networks, exfiltrate sensitive data, and move laterally, impacting both government and private sector organizations. The malicious code was specifically designed to evade detection and enable remote attacker control.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the Orion service starts or the update is installed)
execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (malicious code injected into legitimate DLL)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (when the Orion service starts or the update is installed), the code delays execution for up to two weeks, then collects system and environment information and sends it to a remote command-and-control (C2) server via HTTP, enabling remote attacker control and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is engineered to covertly communicate with an external attacker-controlled server, delay execution for an extended period to evade detection, and enable remote command execution. These behaviors are characteristic of advanced persistent threat (APT) malware and are not present in legitimate SolarWinds Orion code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not contain logic that initiates outbound network connections to unknown or attacker-controlled domains, implements long execution delays for anti-analysis, or executes arbitrary remote commands received from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software update mechanisms may contact vendor servers for update checks, but they do not delay execution for days, communicate with non-SolarWinds domains, or execute arbitrary remote commands.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests from Orion-related processes to avsvmcloud.com or other attacker-controlled domains
Execution delay of 12-14 days after installation or service start (sleep function)
Dynamic code execution based on commands received from remote C2 server
Exfiltration of system and environment information via HTTP POST
Presence of unauthorized code sections within SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the SolarWinds Orion update DLL and distributed to customers via official SolarWinds update channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of backdoor code on customer systems

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or service start, the malicious DLL loads and delays execution for up to two weeks to avoid detection by security tools and analysts.
The backdoor collects system and environment data from the infected host and sends it to the attacker's C2 server via HTTP.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains situational awareness and remote access

attack_chain.action: The attacker issues commands to the infected system through the C2 channel, enabling lateral movement, data theft, or further compromise of the network.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full attacker control and potential data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: Delayed execution (sleep for 12-14 days) after installation or service start by Orion-related processes
Outbound HTTP requests from SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll to suspicious or newly registered domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Unexpected network activity originating from Orion-related processes, especially to non-SolarWinds domains
Dynamic code execution in Orion processes based on remote commands received over HTTP
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unauthorized or unexpected code sections
DLLs with digital signatures or hashes that do not match official SolarWinds releases
Unusual modifications or unexpected files within the SolarWinds Orion installation directory
network_indicators: Outbound connections to avsvmcloud.com and other attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure
HTTP POST requests containing system or environment data from Orion-related hosts
DNS queries for attacker-controlled domains associated with Sunburst C2 activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SolarWinds Orion installations for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to domains not associated with SolarWinds (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Analyze SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll for unauthorized code changes, mismatched hashes, or altered digital signatures. Look for delayed execution patterns (sleeping for days) and dynamic command execution in Orion processes. Correlate endpoint telemetry, file integrity monitoring, and network traffic with known C2 domains and file indicators to identify compromised systems.
